blocks.text: You can configure PingOne SSO as the authentication method for the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform), allowing users to sign in through your PingOne SSO provider, instead of using a username and password. To do this, you can specify a domain, and users with email addresses matching that domain are redirected to authenticate through PingOne. Each user must have an account with the same email address in both the Agentic SecOps Platform and PingOne. After SSO is enabled for a domain, it becomes the only authentication method for the Agentic SecOps Platform.
To configure PingOne SSO, complete the following steps:

blocks.item: Step 1: Generate SAML Details
To set up SSO account authentication, you must generate a SAML Entity ID and Reply URL within the Agentic SecOps Platform. To learn more, see Generating SAML Details.
Step 2: Create an Application Portal Link

The Agentic SecOps Platform doesn't natively support identity provider (IdP)-initiated login. Instead, implement the following process using an Application Portal Link app that redirects to app.avalor.io.
Log in to the Ping Identity admin center.
In the Applications menu, click Application Portal.
See image.
On the Application Portal page, click the Add icon to add a new link.
See image.
In the Add Link window:
Link Name: Enter a name for the application portal.
Description: Add a description.
Icon: Upload a logo from your system.
URL: Enter https://app.avalor.io?domain=<Your Org Domain>, replacing <Your Org Domain> with your actual organization domain.
See image.
Click Save.
Step 3: Register an Application

After generating SAML details, you can register an application in the Ping Identity admin center to define how your application interacts with the Agentic SecOps Platform. The application registration process is performed within the centralized PingOne admin center.
Log in to the Ping Identity admin center.
In the Applications menu, click Applications.
See image.
On the Applications page, click the + icon.
See image.
In the Application Name field, enter Agentic SecOps Platform- Authentication Only.
Use the attached Agentic SecOps Platform logo as the application icon.
Under Choose Application Type, select SAML Application.
See image.
In the SAML Application window, click Configure.
See image.
The SAML Configuration page appears.
On the SAML Configuration page:
Under Provide Application Metadata, select Manually Enter.
Under ACS URLs, enter the Reply URL you copied from the Agentic SecOps Platform.
For Entity ID, enter the Entity ID you copied from the Agentic SecOps Platform.
See image.
Click Save.
Go to the Attribute Mappings tab.
See image.
Click the Edit icon next to Attributes.
The Edit Attribute Mappings page appears.
On the Edit Attribute Mappings page:
Under Attributes, enter http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress.
From the PingOne Mappings drop-down menu, select Email Address.
Select the Required checkbox.
See image.
Click Save.
Go to the Access tab.
See image.
Click the Edit icon next to Attributes.
On the Edit Access page, deselect Display this application in the Application Portal.
See image.
Click Save.
Step 4: Share Metadata with Zscaler
After registering an app in the Ping Identity admin center, share XML metadata with your Zscaler Account team.
Go to the Configuration tab.
See image.
Click Download Metadata.
To share metadata with Zscaler:
In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, and click Account Settings.
In the Authenticate section, paste the XML metadata into the SAML XML MetaData field.
If the Authenticate section is not visible, share the XML metadata with your Zscaler Account team.
See image.
While a metadata URL is also supported, Zscaler recommends pasting the XML metadata directly.
